rules._description: CCC > 30 days indicates liquidity trapped in trade cycle lag
rules.out_rationale: 'Cash is trapped in working capital for {ccc_days} days. Customer payment collection (DSO: {dso_days}d) lags vendor payment terms (DPO: {dpo_days}d). Invoice factoring or a working capital facility is recommended.'

rules._description: CCC between 0 and 30 days reflects balanced trade terms
rules.out_rationale: 'Working capital cycle is balanced at {ccc_days} days. Customer collection and vendor payment schedules align.'

rules._description: Negative CCC means suppliers fund operations before customer collections
rules.out_rationale: 'Negative working capital cycle ({ccc_days} days). Vendor credit terms finance receivables before client collections.'

rules._description: WCR days > 60 flags severe working capital trap
rules.out_rationale: 'Working capital requirement exceeds 60 days of operations.'

rules._description: WCR <= 0 dollars means cash generative float
rules.out_rationale: 'Negative working capital requirement: operations generate net float.'

rules._description: DSO 0 days indicates instant customer collections
rules.out_rationale: 'Instant payment on fulfillment. Zero customer credit risk.'

rules._description: DSO 999 indicates zero credit sales with outstanding AR
rules.out_rationale: 'Outstanding receivables with zero recent credit sales. High default likelihood.'

rules._description: DSO <= 30 days indicates efficient billing and collections
rules.out_rationale: 'Disciplined customer receivables turnover under 30 days.'

rules._description: DSO 31-60 days is commercial standard
rules.out_rationale: 'Commercial standard 30 to 60 day payment terms.'

rules._description: DSO > 60 days flags collection delay
rules.out_rationale: 'Collection delay exceeding 60 days. Risk of cash flow constriction.'

rules._description: DPO > 90 days indicates supplier trade distress
rules.out_rationale: 'Payables stretched beyond 90 days. Indicates supplier strain or liquidity conservation.'

rules._description: DPO 30-90 days is balanced commercial float
rules.out_rationale: 'Standard commercial trade payable float (30 to 90 days).'

rules._description: DPO < 30 days indicates short supplier float
rules.out_rationale: 'Early vendor payment cycle under 30 days. Minimal trade credit captured.'

rules._description: DIR >= 90 days indicates robust liquidity buffer
rules.out_rationale: 'Robust liquidity buffer ({value} days). Operations secure without new receipts.'

rules._description: DIR 30-89 days indicates standard commercial buffer
rules.out_rationale: 'Standard commercial buffer ({value} days). Normal operational cushion.'

rules._description: DIR 15-29 days indicates tight liquidity reserve
rules.out_rationale: 'Tight liquidity reserve ({value} days). Vulnerable to customer payment delays.'

rules._description: DIR < 15 days indicates acute insolvency danger
rules.out_rationale: 'Acute insolvency danger ({value} days). Liquid assets depleted in under 15 days.'

rules._description: Operating cash flow ratio >= 1.0x indicates strong solvency
rules.out_rationale: 'Strong short-term solvency ({value}x). Operating cash flow covers current liabilities.'

rules._description: Operating cash flow ratio 0.5-0.99x indicates adequate coverage
rules.out_rationale: 'Moderate coverage ({value}x). Dependent on rolling credit facilities or vendor float.'

rules._description: Operating cash flow ratio 0.0-0.49x indicates weak liquidity
rules.out_rationale: 'Weak liquidity ({value}x). High debt rollover and refinancing risk.'

rules._description: Operating cash flow ratio < 0.0x indicates operational cash drain
rules.out_rationale: 'Negative operating cash flow ({value}x). Core operations deplete liquidity.'

rules._description: Default balanced baseline
rules.out_rationale: 'Balanced operating working capital position.'
